title: KV metadata sweep + allocator fingerprint hotpatch to stop cross-tenant GPU OOM cascade
creator: Asha Menon
description: Customer escalations across Hosted and Dedicated over the past 48 hours show a correlated increase in GPU OOMs rooted in lingering KV metadata handles and allocator fragmentation. Multiple tenants experienced hard OOMs during bursty traffic; root cause appears to be stale KV index entries (tombstones) that retain small pinned buffers and prevent arena reclamation, combined with a pathological allocation pattern that fragments GPU slabs. This ticket tracks the engineering investigation, the runtime hotpatch (metadata sweep + allocator fingerprinting), and the controlled rollout.
updates: 2026-03-01: Pager alerted on OOM spike in hosted-us-west; oncall triaged to runtime team. Initial mitigation: raised per-tenant soft memory cap and enabled eviction heartbeat throttle to slow allocation rate.

2026-03-02: Reproduced on internal stress harness with synthetic prefix storms. Heap profiler shows thousands of ~64KB pinned allocations referenced only by KV index tombstones created during prefix merges.

2026-03-04: Narrowed failure mode: concurrent prefix compaction left tombstone metadata pointing to ephemeral handles; GC path wasn’t triggering because tombstones were considered live by index referencer.
2026-03-05: Design decision: implement aggressive tombstone retire path (epoch-advance retire) + allocator fingerprinting to identify long-lived pinned allocations for background sweep.
2026-03-07: GH PR 1289 open with runtime patch implementing metadata sweep and allocation fingerprint cache. Catastrophic OOMs prevented in local canary. Integration tests added.
2026-03-09: Canary rollout to 3 small clusters started (hosted-us-west-2a, dedicated-canary-1, private-cust-A test). Metrics: per-cluster OOM events decreased 94% within first 12 hours.
2026-03-10: Observability additions merged: tombstone-age histogram, allocator-fingerprint hit rate, and an automatic alert when fragmentation ratio > 0.35.
Next: Expand rollout to remaining clusters after validation window and prepare customer communications and postmortem writeup.
reproduction_steps: Deploy stress harness that issues many small prefix-updates (mixed creates/deletes) against KV layer while running long-running generation requests to keep KV handles alive.
Monitor allocator arena occupancy with runtime heapprof: look for many small pinned allocations > 30s and tombstone-count spike.
Trigger compaction path by running concurrent background prefix merges to reproduce tombstone retention race.
Observe GPU OOMs after sustained churn when fragmentation ratio exceeds ~0.4 under typical GPU memory sizes (A10/A100).
investigation_notes: Tombstones created during prefix merge path were not retired due to a race in index refcounts; GC considered them live because of transient metadata pointers.
Pinned allocations are small (~32-128KB) but extremely numerous and spread across slab classes, blocking large contiguous allocations needed for KV caches and model tensors.
Allocator does not currently maintain a compacted freelist for slabs with >50% internal fragmentation; fragmentation increases non-linearly under bursty allocation patterns.
Observed cross-tenant amplification: a single noisy tenant causes slab fragmentation that reduces global available contiguous memory, triggering OOMs for co-located tenants on same GPU node.
Leak repro tests showed deterministic reproduction when tombstone retention age > 20s and sustained prefix churn > 200 ops/s.
mitigation_plan: Immediate: enable eviction heartbeat throttle for bursty routes to limit allocation rate and reduce amplification.
Hotpatch: metadata-sweep job that scans KV index for tombstones older than an epoch threshold and advances retire path to allow GC to reclaim handles.
Hotpatch: allocator fingerprinting module that records a compact token (size + class + short backtrace hash) on allocation and triggers background coalescing of classes with many stale tokens.
Rollout plan: canary -> 25% -> 100% with 24h observation windows. Automatic rollback if OOM rate or latency regressions > 10%.
Customer-facing: send interim note to affected customers with recommended mitigation knobs (per-tenant cap) and ETA for hotpatch rollout.
rollout_plan: Canary 1 (3 clusters): hosted-us-west-2a, dedicated-canary-1, private-test-A — verify no regressions for 12h.
Canary 2 (25% fleet): expand to low-traffic regions, monitor OOM-rate, fragmentation-ratio, and 95p latency for 24h.
Full rollout: 100% across hosted and dedicated if metrics stable; schedule private upgrade windows with customers.
Post-rollout: increase retention of fragmentation histograms and tombstone-age metrics for 14 days to detect recurrence.
postmortem_next_steps: Complete postmortem doc with timeline, root cause, and customer impact by 2026-03-20.
Add end-to-end fuzzer for prefix compaction + GC to catch tombstone races before release.
Design longer-term allocator work: slab compaction thread and per-tenant slab quotas to limit cross-tenant amplification.
Add regression tests to CI that simulate bursty churn patterns and assert fragmentation ratio stays < 0.25.
